A 59-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and hypertension visits for a follow-up
blood pressure evaluation. His current blood pressure is 154/73 mm Hg. He began taking
hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily several weeks ago. His other medications include aspirin 81 mg daily,
carvedilol 25 mg twice daily, and simvastatin 40 mg daily. His kidney function and potassium levels
remain within normal limits. Which of the following antihypertensive medications can be safely and
effectively added to his current treatment plan? Answer Choices: (A) Ramipril (B) Spironolactone (C)
Verapamil (D) Clonidine (E) Hydralazine (F) Diltiazem (G) Aliskiren (H) Metoprolol (I) Losartan (J)
Amlodipine
 A. Ramipril
B. Verapamil
C. Spironolactone
D. Aliskiren
E. Clonidine
F. Diltiazem
G. Losartan
H. Amlodipine
I. Hydralazine
J. Metoprolol
